Sochaczew Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sochaczew, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are recorded in Sochaczew from the 15th century; the town became a Hasidic center (Sochatchov Hasidim) in the 19th century, and by 1921, 2,419 Jews made up 48% of the population before deportation to the Warsaw Ghetto in 1941. This cemetery, first documented in 1564, holds the graves of Rabbis Mosze Charif, Eliezer ha-Kohen Lipsker, and Awraham Nachum Bornstein (the first Sochatchover Rebbe) with his family. The last known burial was likely Pinkas Weinberg, the town's vice-mayor and Jewish Committee chairman, murdered on May 20, 1945. Germans used tombstones for airport construction at Bielice during the war; a playground and occasional circus shows occupied the site under Communist rule. Historian Paweł Fijałkowski recovered and restored a dozen matzevot in the 1980s, and from 1989-1992 the Sochaczew Jewish Landsmanshaft (with Jehuda Widawski) fenced the site, added two Holocaust memorials, and rebuilt the Bornstein family ohel.
